topics.title: Association Between Zero-Calorie Beverage Consumption and Suicidality Among Korean Adolescents: A Nationwide Cross-Sectional Study
topics.population: All middle and high school students participating in the 2025 KYRBS (21st wave); students with missing values on exposure, outcome, or key covariates excluded via listwise deletion (after confirming <5% missingness)
topics.rationale: Sugar-sweetened beverage intake has been linked to depression and suicidality in adolescents, but zero-calorie (artificially sweetened) beverages have emerged as a popular alternative among Korean youth. Recent evidence suggests artificial sweeteners may affect gut-brain axis, mood regulation, and reward pathways. With zero_drink_intake newly added in the 2025 KYRBS, this is the first opportunity to examine its association with suicidality at a national scale, informing both clinical and policy guidance on adolescent beverage consumption.
topics.novelty_hint: First nationally representative analysis using the newly introduced 2025 zero_drink_intake variable; distinguishes zero-calorie from sugar-sweetened beverage effects on mental health, addressing a gap where prior Korean studies focused only on sweet_drink_intake. Also examines a dose-response gradient across the full suicidality continuum (ideation→plan→attempt).
topics.suggested_design: Cross-sectional analysis using 2025 KYRBS (single-year, complex survey design)
topics.covariates: sex, grade, school_type, region, family_econ, academic_perf, residence_type, stress, depression, sleep_weekday, pa_60min, bmi_category, sweet_drink_intake, caffeine_intake, breakfast_skip, alc_current, cig_current
topics.analysis_note: Apply complex survey design (svydesign with cluster_id, strata_id, wt, nest=TRUE) and use svyglm with logit link for each binary suicidality outcome. Mutually adjust for sweet_drink_intake and caffeine_intake to isolate zero-beverage-specific effects; check VIF for collinearity among beverage variables. Stratify by sex given known sex differences in adolescent suicidality. Test linear trend across ordinal zero_drink_intake categories. Conduct sensitivity analyses excluding current depression cases to assess reverse causation. Report aORs with 95% CIs and ICC at school level. Acknowledge cross-sectional design limits causal inference and self-report measurement bias.
